summary: Interpreted the new receipt, closing the empty-command finding's client-side consequence with a measurement rather than a derivation. Receipt 098ab4425325464192aa558be557f0ce (fixed experiment 49b316fdc67c459fb374500fb7f26514-experiment) attaches a real client proposal (command id 91) to the owner's own instance, whose own recovery decides the empty batch: both declared comparisons are violated with complete witness 4 - the decided instance holds a command list of length zero although the owner held command X at status ACCEPTED before (index 0), and the owner's pending request is never re-offered (requeued 0 with pending_proposals 1 and reply_bytes 0). Set against the single-NOOP receipt of the same family, where the request was re-queued and later completed, this measures the gap in the re-offer protection: handleCommit requires exactly one command with operation NONE, which an empty batch never satisfies. The account now cites both receipts of the question, the source-derived statement that the re-offer does not fire is replaced by that measurement, and the supporting behavior entry gained the new receipt along with the re-offer condition, so it states the whole decode-adoption-fallback chain in one place: nil becomes an empty slice on the wire, the fallback's nil test passes it through, an empty non-nil batch executes as a no-op, and the re-offer path does not recognise it. Both gaps of the question remain resolved, the experiment binding is refreshed to the new receipt's experiment, and the run's other accounts - five explained questions plus this one, four asserted defects, the holds account, the refuted wrong-row-write result and nine behavior entries - are unchanged. What stays open is narrow and stated: only the owner-as-recoverer case with one pending proposal was exercised, execution-side effects remain source-derived, and the delivery-order variant of the question is still unmeasured.
